newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - June 24.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- President Kim Young-sam and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto Monday agreed to take unified action on food assistance to North Korea.
- With the presidential nomination drawing closer, Lee Hoi-chang and the main stream faction of the ruling camp are staging an all-out brawl to get an upper hand in the nomination race.

- The New Korea Party will have the government make public within the year the list of Korean War prisoners who have not been repatriated by North Korea so that families of the prisoners can have access to it.

- Amid the protracted economic slump and a string of corporate bankruptcies, the nation's tax revenues are likely to fall short of this year's goal by as much as four trillion won, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said.

- In another bare admission of its economic hardship, North Korea has said in a report to a U.N. committee that its per capita gross national product was down from $868 in 1988 to a mere $239 in 1995.
- The opposition party, United Liberal Democrats, will elect its new president and presidential candidate for the December 18 election in a national convention on Tuesday.
